Studded LEGO track laid on plate-built sleepers, the whole bed filled with grey cheese-slope ballast tiles giving the line a textured, dressed-stone roadbed feel.
A SNOT-smooth locomotive body assembled with headlight bricks and jumper plates, tiles facing outward so the flanks read as burnished steel without a single exposed stud.
Brick-built connecting rods and valve-gear linking the large driving wheels, Technic pins and liftarms giving the mechanism genuine reciprocating geometry true to a steam outline.
Ornate viaduct piers built from castle-wall masonry bricks, each arch spanning with curved brick sections and coped along the top with a row of cheese-slope crestings.
A sloped-brick locomotive nose assembled from a run of 2x2 and 1x2 slopes in dark-red, the tapered form narrowing cleanly toward the front buffer beam.
Trans-clear plates mortared into brick frames along each carriage side, producing a continuous ribbon of glazing that catches the interior lamp studs as warm amber glow.
Greebled cab interior furnished with a round-tile boiler pressure gauge, a 1x1 clip-brick throttle lever and a minifigure-scale coal heap in dark-grey slope bricks.
Lineside signal posts built from round-stud bricks topped with a bracket plate, trans-red and trans-green 1x1 round tiles acting as the working lamp lenses.
Stone-brick tunnel portals assembled in light-bluish-grey, the arch keystones picked out in tan bricks and the wingwalls battered inward with plate offsets for convincing masonry depth.
Plant-element foliage pushed onto studs along the embankment edge, mixed-green leaf parts and round flower plates tumbling down the slope-brick cutting side toward the track bed.
A brick-built water tower with a round-brick barrel section, the tank tapered with wedge plates at the base and a flex-tube spout hanging over the track.
Crossing gates assembled from bar-and-clip hinge bricks, striped with alternating red-and-white tile plates and mounted on a brick-built post flanking the studded level-crossing plates.
Tender bodywork built up from stacked plates with a jumper-plate coal load, the dark-grey slopes representing heaped fuel visible above the brick-sided coal bunker walls.
Boiler barrel courses laid as a stack of round 4x4 ring bricks, each course offset slightly in tan to suggest riveted iron-plate construction along the loco backbone.
Brick-built platform edging using yellow-stripe tile plates over a raised plate deck, lamp-post rounds rising at regular intervals with trans-yellow 1x1 stud globes at the crown.
Slope-brick cutting walls angled back on each side of the line, light-tan and grey slopes interspersed with green plate vegetation pushing through the brick-rock face.
A locomotive smoke-deflector pair built from flat SNOT plates mounted on bracket bricks, the smooth tile faces presenting clean slab sides framing the boiler front.
Carriage interior detail built on a base plate, bench seating in reddish-brown tiles, a 1x1 round headrest brick and luggage-rack bar elements above each seat row.
Stone-brick bridge abutments stepped back in successive plate layers, the reveals deepening with each course to cast strong shadow lines across the brick-textured riverside face.
Trans-blue plate river surface laid in overlapping offset layers below the viaduct, dark-blue cheese slopes along the banks suggesting depth where brick water meets brick stone.
Brick-built station canopy using roof-slope elements on a grid of round-brick columns, the underside SNOT-tiled in white to present a smooth vault above the platform.
A parts-built locomotive headlamp assembled from a round-brick housing, a trans-yellow domed stud inside and a chrome-finish 1x1 cone protruding as the polished reflector.
Goods-wagon bodywork planked with tan 1x4 tiles over a plate frame, the doors represented by recessed jumper plates and clip-brick drop-bar fastenings along the sides.
Brick-built engine-shed walls in dark-red with arched doorways formed from curved 1x3 bricks, the roof clad in overlapping dark-grey slope tiles suggesting Welsh slate.
Trackside linesman's hut assembled from printed-window bricks, a slope-brick roof in dark-green and a SNOT-smooth chimney stack of round bricks rising from the rear wall.
